title: Deterministic read routing and quarantine queues for tenant-local analytics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Context: Console analytics currently fans telemetry and usage events across regions in a best-effort fashion. For some regulated tenants we must ensure read traffic for analytics dashboards and alerting hits region-local aggregates or a deterministically pinned replica, and that cross-border events are subject to quarantine and legal classification before replication. Problem: we observed a production incident where a misrouted ingest stream caused a short window of cross-border replication for a tenant under a residency contract (Incident: IN-2025-03-02-analytics-routemiss). Goals: 1) Provide deterministic read routing so reads (dashboard queries, trend computations) prefer tenant-local materialized views with a bounded-staleness fallback; 2) Introduce quarantine queues and a lightweight policy engine that tags, holds, and routes cross-border events for manual review or automated gating based on legal tags; 3) Ensure we have observable SLOs for data locality and bounded staleness, with clear rollback. Non-goals: full re-architect of analytics storage; this ticket implements routing and gating surface and integration hooks for the replication controller. This ticket covers console backend orchestration and pipeline hooks only; storage layer changes are tracked separately. Current progress: prototype routing middleware implemented in console-backend v2, integration tests added for deterministic hash and tenant tag evaluation, quarantine queue proof-of-concept using existing Kafka topic with TTL. Open PRs and design doc linked below. Decision notes: prefe r a routing-on-read model over routing-on-write to minimize ingestion throughput changes; use tenant-scoped materialized views as primary read target and allow a bounded-staleness replica (max intended lag 5 minutes) as fallback. Expect follow-up work to tighten staleness or implement stronger geo-partitioned storage if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Reads for tenants with 'local-only' residency tag are routed to tenant-local materialized views by default
A bounded-staleness fallback (configurable, default 5m) is used when local view is unavailable
Cross-border events are written to a quarantine topic with tenant/legal classification metadata before any replication to other regions
Policy engine supports at least two actions: automatic-release after TTL, and manual-approval via console
End-to-end tests and a canary rollout plan exist; dashboard shows data-locality ratio and staleness percentiles
proposed_solution: Implement a deterministic read router component in console-backend that computes a tenancy hash and resolves to the preferred region/replica based on tenant residency metadata. On ingest, introduce a quarantine dispatcher: events whose tenant tag requires residency review are written to quarantine Kafka topic with classification headers. A lightweight policy engine (policy rules stored in config DB) decides whether to mark events 'release' or 'hold'. Release flows trigger existing replication controller hooks; hold flows surface items in a Console review UI (separate PR). The router will expose an HTTP header (X-Local-Replica: region-id, staleness-ms) for downstream services to make informed fallback decisions. We will reuse existing Kafka and consumer groups for quarantine processing and avoid creating new storage services in this phase.
tradeoffs: Routing-on-read keeps ingest throughput stable but increases read latency for lookups to routing service
Quarantine topic preserves safety but adds an operational queue to monitor; introduces possible replication delays
Bounded-staleness fallback trades strict locality for availability; documented as tenant SLA tradeoff
Storing policy rules in config DB is simpler for rollout but less expressive than a full policy language
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deployment to staging with synthetic tenants (mar-12). 2) Canary: route 1% of production reads for non-residency tenants to validate router logic (mar-18). 3) Pilot with two residency customers in us-west-2 only (mar-25). 4) Expand to additional regions after monitoring SLOs and customer sign-off (apr-01). Rollback: disable routing feature flag and drain quarantine topic consumers. Manual rollback playbook documented in attachments.
monitoring_and_alerting: alert: locality_drop (>3% regression over baseline) P0
SLO: 95th percentile staleness for fallback <= 5m for pilot tenants
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for deterministic hashing and tenant tag resolution
Integration test: end-to-end ingest -> quarantine -> release path
Chaos test: simulate regional replica outage and validate bounded-staleness fallback behavior
Compliance test: generate audit trail entries for any cross-border release action
